aboutPage.headline: I like turning messy problems into usable systems.
aboutPage.positioningP1: I’m Daru, a digital product builder, not just a web developer. My work sits at the intersection of product strategy, full-stack development, AI, UI/UX, and brand design. Most projects I take on need more than one of those disciplines to actually work, so I don’t separate them too strictly. I use whichever one is necessary to turn a problem into something usable.
aboutPage.positioningP1Lead: I’m Daru, a digital product builder, not just a web developer. My work sits at the intersection of product strategy, full-stack development, AI, UI/UX, and brand design.
aboutPage.positioningP1Rest: Most projects I take on need more than one of those disciplines to actually work, so I don’t separate them too strictly. I use whichever one is necessary to turn a problem into something usable.
aboutPage.positioningP2: A lot of what I’ve built comes from friction I ran into firsthand, or friction people around me kept running into:
aboutPage.positioningP3: That’s why the work in this portfolio ranges from an AI assistant for Indonesian students in Egypt, to a payment-integrated fiqh course platform, to an internal operations system for a travel agency, to brand identities for bakeries and laundry services. Different domains, same approach: find the real problem, decide what discipline it actually needs, and build it end to end.
aboutPage.howIWorkP1: Most projects here were handled end to end, from the original problem and product thinking, through visual identity, to the shipped, deployed product. That includes client work, where the brief comes from someone else’s operation, and personal/community projects, where the brief starts with something I ran into myself.
aboutPage.howIWorkP2: I’m explicit on this portfolio about what stage each project is actually at: production, in development, pre-launch, concept, or delivered to a client, because I think a portfolio should be honest about what’s real and what’s still in progress.
